A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Adaptive Message Passing (AMP) work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original AMP experiments on three synthetic graph tasks and two peptide benchmarks, together with message-filtering ablations and diagnostic analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original AMP benchmark results and reports additional node-classification experiments and peptide ablations in Appendices F, I, and J.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure retains adaptive truncated-depth distributions, input- or embedding-based sigmoid message filtering, ELBO optimization, and weighted predictions across layers. The folded-normal and mixture families already appear in v2. Expanded mathematical exposition and fixed-depth ablations do not establish a change to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix F adds node classification on Texas, Wisconsin, Actor, Squirrel, Chameleon, Citeseer, Pubmed, and Cora, covering graphs with substantially different homophily levels. This broadens task and data coverage beyond the retained Diameter, SSSP, Eccentricity, peptides-func, and peptides-struct benchmarks.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds PH-DGN and IPR-MPNN to the peptide comparison. The new node-classification Table 3 includes additional comparators such as H2GCN-1/2, GCN-Cheby, MixHop, several jumping-knowledge variants, GEOM-GCN, and MLP. The synthetic comparator set in Table 1 is unchanged; methods such as NBA and CO-GNN already appeared in v2.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a node-classification protocol with cited Zhu splits, embedding/depth searches, 2000 maximum epochs, and patience 250, plus encoding-removal and fixed-depth controls. It also changes the stated peptides-struct weight-prior covariance from 10I to I. Existing benchmark splits and primary metrics remain unchanged. The sensitivity sum changes its index from edges to V, although the intended node-pair set is unclear.

E4.justification: Appendix I/Table 5 newly tests dependence on positional and structural encodings. Appendix J/Table 6 tests fixing depth after selecting a range informed by AMP, while holding other hyperparameters at their selected values. These directly examine two important sources of performance. The earlier message-filtering ablation, learned-depth analysis, and prediction case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over 20 synthetic runs and four peptide runs, and retain prediction error bands. The new peptide ablations use the same four-run reporting practice. No new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedure is specified.

E6.justification: Table 1 is unchanged, but all three AMP peptide rows are revised. For example, AMP GINE AP changes from 0.7011 to 0.7065, and AMP GCN MAE from 0.2431 to 0.2446; these are revised results, with a changed stated prior for peptides-struct. Newly listed IPR-MPNN has the best Table 2 means, 0.7210 AP and 0.2422 MAE. Node-classification and encoding/depth-ablation results are added, and sensitivity curves are updated.

T1.justification: v3 adds Theorem 3.1 and its proof, bounding Jacobian sensitivity using filtering derivatives, filter magnitudes, adjacency, and depth. The distribution theorems and approximate message-propagation proof are retained in Appendices B and D. However, the new short Theorem 3.2 states exact equality, whereas its retained appendix formulation guarantees only arbitrarily close approximation.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the performance claim from surpassing the state of the art to competing with it. The introduction adds the sensitivity-bound result as an explicit theoretical contribution. The central claim that jointly learning depth and message filtering improves graph prediction remains.

C2.justification: v3 removes v2 Section 8's substantive discussion of multi-message propagation constraints, fixed embedding-width limitations, and observed training instability. Parameter overhead remains discussed. New interpretations address dependence on encodings, the value of adaptive versus fixed depth, and why homophily does not establish a long-range task. Much of the original oversquashing discussion is retained in Appendix D.

D1.justification: Appendix E newly specifies previously referenced settings, including learning rates, weight decay, embedding dimensions, readout depth, dropout placement, batch size, and epoch limits. v3 also specifies 250 validation nodes for sensitivity calculations. Conversely, it removes the PyDGN/OGB implementation disclosures and the optimizer-state reset detail. The code-access link remains the same.

R1.justification: v3 adds positioning against graph state-space and randomized-signature approaches, including Wang, Toth, and Gruber, and cites newer comparisons such as PH-DGN and IPR-MPNN. Some background and software references disappear. Most existing research positioning survives in Appendix A; publication updates to retained methods do not constitute new related work.

P1.justification: The journal-style exposition is substantially condensed and reorganized into a conference paper. The introduction, related-work summary, method explanation, and conclusion are rewritten; distribution theory, derivations, experimental details, and prediction analyses move into appendices. The dedicated limitations section is removed.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column journal layout to a two-column conference layout. Figures are resized and restyled, and captions substantially shortened. v2 Figure 7 is split into v3 Figures 4 and 9. Table 2 expands, and new Tables 3, 5, and 6 present classification and ablation results; other displays are largely retained or relocated.

improvement.justification: The new depth and encoding ablations strengthen validation, while explicit hyperparameters improve reproducibility. However, v3 removes substantive limitations and introduces an exact-recovery statement in Theorem 3.2 inconsistent with its approximate appendix guarantee. Its blanket improvement claim and Table 2 dagger also persist despite AMP GatedGCN's peptides-struct MAE of 0.2480 versus the base model's 0.2477. These gains and losses in qualification and internal consistency prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
